turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. You asked for this meeting, so start talking. I have a client call at 4:40.
Okay. Owen found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class. What do you have to tell me?
This meeting is over. I'm leaving.
You asked for this meeting, and you're not walking out of it. Withdraw the zero, or I'm going to the principal's office next.

Sit down, Hale. You put a zero in the gradebook before anyone called me, and you don't get to end this by walking out. Tell me what you have on Owen's essay, or the principal hears it from me in five minutes.
Because you haven't answered a single question. Procedure 4.2 says a parent is contacted before any mark goes in, and nobody contacted me. So, Hale: what do you have, and who decided on that zero?
